title: Sinomenine Modifies Parkinson's Disease Through Nrf2 Activation.
authors: Zhu, Lingling; Lin, Lin; Yang, Zhenyu; Tang, Hongxia; Wu, Jinping; Kang, Zeyi; Feng, Yi; Zheng, Binbin; Hu, Qirou; Wang, Shanshan; Liu, Cuimin; Jiang, Zhengli; Liu, Suzhi; Wu, Gang
one_liner_zh: 该文研究青藤碱通过Nrf2/ARE通路改善帕金森病，仅含分子对接辅助验证，核心为细胞/动物实验，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Disease-modifying treatments for Parkinson's disease (PD) are urgently needed, with the Nrf2/ARE pathway a promising target. This study aims to explore the effects of sinomenine on PD and Nrf2/ARE activation. METHODS: 6-OHDA-treated Parkinsonian SH-SY5Y cells and rats were used. Apoptosis and cell viability were measured using flow cytometry and CCK-8 assays. Nrf2 and its downstream proteins were assessed by Western blotting, while ROS levels were detected with fluorescent dyes. Nrf2 silencing via shRNA evaluated sinomenine's dependence on Nrf2 activation. In vivo, behavioral changes, tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) levels and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels were measured. Microglial inflammation was analyzed by measuring TNF-alpha and IL-1beta expression and cytoskeleton analysis. Nrf2 nuclear translocation was verified by Western blotting and molecular docking was performed. RESULTS: Sinomenine reduced apoptosis and ROS, improved cell viability, upregulated Nrf2 and antioxidant enzyme expression. The protective effects against apoptosis were abolished by Nrf2 silencing. In PD animals, sinomenine improved motor deficits, enhanced Nrf2, GCLC, GCLM, NQO1, and HO-1 expression, decreased MDA levels, increased TH levels in the striatum and maintained count of dopaminergic neurons in substantia nigra. Additionally, it suppressed TNF-alpha and IL-1beta levels in brain tissue and blood, preserving normal microglial morphology and reducing neuroinflammation. Sinomenine promoted Nrf2 nuclear translocation and showed high Keap1 affinity in docking. CONCLUSIONS: Sinomenine activates the Nrf2/ARE pathway, mitigating oxidative stress and inflammation in PD models, possibly through Keap1 binding and Nrf2 nuclear translocation. These findings suggest sinomenine may serve as a potential disease-modifying therapy for Parkinson's disease, pending further clinical validation.
abstract_zh: 背景：帕金森病（Parkinson's disease, PD）的疾病修饰治疗亟需开发，其中Nrf2/ARE通路是一个有前景的靶点。本研究旨在探讨青藤碱（sinomenine）对PD及Nrf2/ARE激活的影响。方法：使用6-OHDA处理的帕金森病SH-SY5Y细胞和大鼠模型。通过流式细胞术和CCK-8实验测量细胞凋亡和细胞活力。利用Western blotting评估Nrf2及其下游蛋白，而ROS水平则通过荧光染料检测。通过shRNA沉默Nrf2评估青藤碱对Nrf2激活的依赖性。在体内实验中，测量行为变化、酪氨酸羟化酶（tyrosine hydroxylase, TH）水平和丙二醛（malondialdehyde, MDA）水平。通过测量TNF-α和IL-1β表达及细胞骨架分析来评估小胶质细胞炎症。通过Western blotting验证Nrf2核转位，并进行分子对接。结果：青藤碱减少凋亡和ROS，提高细胞活力，上调Nrf2及抗氧化酶表达。Nrf2沉默消除了其对凋亡的保护作用。在PD动物中，青藤碱改善运动缺陷，增强Nrf2、GCLC、GCLM、NQO1和HO-1表达，降低MDA水平，增加纹状体中TH水平，并维持黑质中多巴胺能神经元数量。此外，它抑制脑组织和血液中TNF-α和IL-1β水平，保持正常小胶质细胞形态并减少神经炎症。青藤碱促进Nrf2核转位，并在对接中显示高Keap1亲和力。结论：青藤碱激活Nrf2/ARE通路，减轻PD模型中的氧化应激和炎症，可能通过Keap1结合和Nrf2核转位实现。这些发现表明，青藤碱可能作为帕金森病的潜在疾病修饰疗法，有待进一步临床验证。
